- When sentiment is neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >90), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in subsequent periods.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price drops below 70, forecast tends to stay low; adjust upward if recent history shows recovery.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates downward trends after 80–85; add 2–5% buffer to avoid under-shock.
- If sentiment includes positive signals (e.g., 0.20), model tends to overreact; cap forecast growth to avoid over-optimism.
- Model often lags in recognizing early trend reversals; add 1–2 day buffer for downward corrections.
- When history shows volatility >10% in 7-day window, reduce forecast volatility by 30% to avoid overfitting.
